title: The launch playbook.
description: How two B2B companies launched on LinkedIn, the real numbers, and the five days of work before either post existed.
formHeader: Two B2B launches. One playbook. Both sets of numbers.
formEyebrow: Get it free, in your inbox

blocks.text: In June a client launched to 181,619 impressions and 137 hours of video watch time. In August another filled his waitlist in under 24 hours. Same playbook, and most of it ran in the five days before either post existed.
Almost everyone treats the post as the launch. The post is about a fifth of it.

The part that decides the outcome is unglamorous. A list of fifty people who would genuinely be pleased for you, messaged personally four days out, each one followed by a calendar invite for launch hour. The ask is always the same three words: like, comment, save. Save is the one people skip and the strongest of the three.

Then there is the mechanic that surprised me. The August launch asked for two actions rather than one: comment below, and fill in the form. 554 people clicked the link. 343 commented. Those are two separate funnels, and most of the qualified signups never touched the link at all. A post that only says "sign up here" gets the 554 and nothing else.

Everything in the document has a number against it, including the parts that went badly. Three weeks after his launch the same founder posted something motivational. It did 72,031 impressions, nearly double the launch, and produced seven followers and no signups.

blocks.text: The honest limit, stated inside the document too: this is two launches, not a law. Both B2B, both founder led, both with an existing network willing to spend four days asking people personally. Skip that part and you get the reach your account already had.
